name: HyperFlow H3 Flash
cost: Code is free (Apache 2.0). The model weights come under the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement
works_with: Its own Python CLI and diffusers, ComfyUI, Unsloth Studio, stable-diffusion.cpp
short: An open video model that makes clips with synced stereo audio from a prompt, an image or references, in 4 to 8 steps.
what: HyperFlow H3 Flash is Video Rebirth's compressed, few-step version of MiniMax-H3. It makes 5.2 to 15 seconds of 24 fps video with a 32 kHz stereo soundtrack. It does text to video, first and last keyframe to video, and up to 12 references. The transformer is about 14B parameters, less than half the original, and comes as GGUF or INT8.
who: People with a strong NVIDIA GPU who run video models locally, in ComfyUI or Python. If you don't have at least a 24 GB card or a data-center GPU, skip it for now. The README says 16 GB GPUs are not measured yet.
needs: An Ampere or newer NVIDIA GPU. The README measures 24 GB and 32 GB RTX cards and H100 to B300
For the Python package: Python 3.10+, PyTorch 2.6+ with CUDA and Triton, and `diffusers >= 0.40`
16 GB+ of system RAM, and much more (about 69 to 91 GiB) if the Python package offloads to RAM
Room for a first download of about 90 GB, or about 68 GB with the fp8 text encoder
Linux or WSL2 for more than one GPU

steps.title: Pick a runtime
steps.text: The README's rule: in ComfyUI on 24 GB+ RTX GPUs use the INT8 safetensors. Use GGUF on smaller GPUs and in stable-diffusion.cpp or Unsloth Studio. Use the INT8 Python package on data-center GPUs, or on 24 GB+ RTX GPUs with at least 69 GiB of system RAM.

steps.title: Make a clip from text
steps.text: The first run downloads the weights, and the Triton kernels take about a minute to compile.
steps.code:
hyperflow-h3-flash --prompt "A chef slides a steaming bowl of ramen across a wooden counter; rain taps on the window." \
    --output ramen.mp4

steps.title: Trade speed for quality
steps.text: `--steps` takes 4 for speed, 6 (the default) or 8 for quality.

steps.title: Or use ComfyUI with GGUF
steps.text: Clone ComfyUI-GGUF and ComfyUI-HyperFlow-Flash into `ComfyUI/custom_nodes/`, download the 15.7 GB `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq` text encoder, then pick a template under Workflow, Browse Templates, ComfyUI-HyperFlow-Flash. On 16 GB or 32 GB PCs start ComfyUI with `python main.py --fast-disk`. The full guide is `integrations/README.md`.

try.label: From the README
try.text: hyperflow-h3-flash --prompt "A chef slides a steaming bowl of ramen across a wooden counter; rain taps on the window." --output ramen.mp4

watch: Using the weights means accepting the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement. The README says it does not cover use in the European Union, the United Kingdom, the Republic of Korea or the United States without MiniMax's authorization, and it includes an Acceptable Use Policy. Read the model card first.
The first run downloads about 90 GB.
Speeds in the README are for big GPUs: a 5.2 second clip takes 92 seconds on one RTX 5090 and 36 seconds on one H200.
The ComfyUI node folder is GPL-3.0 and the stable-diffusion.cpp patch is MIT. The rest of the code is Apache 2.0.
